balance.note: static data ratio is 531:131 (about 4:1) and scores well, so a ~4:1 ratio alone is NOT the root cause. The independent units here are CAPTURES, not flows.

label_noise.note: every flow inherits its capture's label, so ordinary background traffic inside a malware capture is labelled malware. Identical flows with opposite labels cap the best possible flow-level score.

features.note: if almost no single feature separates the classes, flow statistics alone are weak evidence; tiny flows (DNS, handshakes) look the same for any app.

split_effect.note: the gap is how much a random split would have flattered the model by letting near-identical flows of one capture sit on both sides.

unit_of_analysis.note: if capture-level AUC is clearly higher, the weak link is classifying ONE flow; classify the whole capture instead (src/models/train_capture_level.py).
